articles.description: 'Is this simply the price of geopolitical risk or is something else influencing the value of oil?' analysts at J.P. Morgan asked.

articles.title: Eni begins execution phase of Cronos gas project in Cyprus
articles.description: Eni finalised key contracts for the engineering, procurement, construction and drilling of the Cronos gas project located offshore Cyprus.

articles.title: Ovintiv to buy Canadian upstream company Logan Energy for $890m
articles.description: US-based Ovintiv has agreed to acquire Canadian exploration and production company Logan Energy in a deal worth around C$1.26bn ($890m).

articles.title: Investors From 119 Countries Pile Into Dangote’s Record Refinery IPO
articles.description: The initial public offering of Nigeria’s Dangote refinery has reached its target to raise $1.6 billion in funds from domestic and retail investors alone, sources with knowledge of the IPO process told Bloomberg on Tuesday. Demand from international investors is set to significantly exceed even the $2.1-billion target with a 30% over-allotment option, according to the sources. The Dangote refinery is going public as Africa’s richest man, Aliko Dangote, is targeting 10 million retail investors in the “IPO for the people” pitch…

articles.title: Egypt Agrees Tax Relief for Project to Import Cyprus Gas
articles.description: The Chevron-led Aphrodite consortium and the Egyptian government have agreed on a special tax regime for a project that would enable the piped export of 100 percent of production from the field offshore Cyprus to the North African country.

articles.title: Ras Tanura Fire Follows Attacks on Aramco Offices and Near Shaybah Field
articles.description: A fire broke out near Saudi Arabia’s key oil export hub of Ras Tanura on the Persian Gulf following an attack early on Tuesday, but the Kingdom quickly contained the fire, an unnamed source familiar with the events told Bloomberg. The extent of the damage was not clear, nor whether the hub was affected. Saudi Arabia early on Tuesday said it had intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis toward the Eastern Region, as well as four UAVs launched by the militia toward its Southern Region. Attacks have intensified…

articles.title: Aramco Closes In on $10B Loan
articles.description: The Saudi Arabian state-backed oil company is nearing agreement with international banks on a $10 billion loan that would bolster its finances as conflicts in the Middle East threaten crude exports.

articles.title: Equinor and Aker BP partner on tight reservoir development in Norway
articles.description: Equinor and Aker BP have announced a strategic collaboration aimed at developing tight oil and gas reservoirs on the NCS.

articles.title: Diesel Drives India's Fuel Export Windfall as Earnings Reach $12.6 Billion
articles.description: Soaring diesel and gasoline prices hiked the value of India’s fuel exports by 50% between April and September, while the world was grappling with the worst of the Middle East crisis so far. India earned 2.59 trillion Indian rupees, or $27.2 billion, from fuel exports in the six months to September, per oil ministry data cited by The Economic Times. The surge in rupee terms was 50% compared to the same period last year, also driven by the weakening Indian currency against the U.S. dollar. The value of diesel, gasoline, and other fuel exports…

articles.title: India Rejects Claims of U.S. Pressure Over Russian Oil Purchases
articles.description: The United States has not pressured India to cut crude oil imports from Russia, Indian Oil Minister Hardeep Singh Puri said on Tuesday, as Russian cargo arrivals to the world’s third-largest crude oil importer have declined in recent weeks amid an increase in imports from the Middle East. India’s purchases of Russian crude oil are closely linked to the pricing, discounts, and import costs of various grades, the minister said at an industry event. “I never felt anything,” the official said in response to a question about…

articles.title: Trump Moves to Ease Methane Regulations for U.S. Oil Producers
articles.description: The Trump Administration is set to announce easing of the federal methane regulations for oil and gas production in a bid to boost U.S. domestic energy production and lower costs for producers and consumers. President Donald Trump is set to unveil the proposal at a campaign rally in Lubbock, Texas, America’s biggest-oil producing state. The top U.S. oil industry lobby, the American Petroleum Institute (API), and many oil and gas companies have long called for changes to the Biden administration’s 2024 methane emissions standards, arguing…

articles.title: IEA Warns of Dangerous Concentration in Global Clean Energy Supply Chains
articles.description: The global energy transition depends on highly concentrated supply chains, the head of the International Energy Agency, Fatih Birol, has warned, declining to name any of the countries involved in these chains. China is by far the most dominant global player in energy transition technology, capacity, and investment. China makes the most wind and solar equipment, is the biggest battery maker in the world, and also the biggest manufacturer and seller of electric cars. According to Birol, this could be a problem, especially for Southeast Asia, Reuters…

articles.title: India’s Oil Buyers Squeezed by $123 Crude and Weak Rupee
articles.description: The Indian crude basket hit $123.29 per barrel last week, approaching levels recorded in March 2012, and adding 86% to the price Indian oil marketing companies pay, local media have reported, also noting the effect of a cheaper rupee. Since Indian companies pay for the oil they buy from abroad in U.S. dollars, a weaker Indian currency swells the bill further. The combination of a war premium on international oil prices and a weak rupee caused Indian fuel marketers to lose money despite the increase in gasoline and diesel prices, the Financial Express…

articles.title: Oil Prices Drop Despite Threat of New U.S. Strikes on Iran
articles.description: Crude oil prices moved lower today after reports about renewed diplomatic efforts to achieve peace in the Middle East, with Saudi, Turkish, and Pakistani officials travelling to Tehran to discuss the prospects of an end to hostilities. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $114.85 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $100.87 per barrel. That’s down from over $117 for Brent crude at the end of last week, and over $103 for WTI, on peace hopes and traders taking profit. However, continued Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure…

articles.title: Oil Dips from 6 Month High as Officials Meet in Tehran
articles.description: Oil retreated from a six-month high as senior officials from several countries flew to Tehran.

articles.title: Pentagon's Venezuelan Oil Partner Boosts Output
articles.description: Venezuela's overall oil output recently reached 1.252 million barrels a day, oil minister Hector Obregon said.

articles.title: UK Weighs Scrapping Its Largest Untapped Oilfield With Oil Over $100
articles.description: Britain is deciding whether to drill its largest untapped oilfield in the middle of an oil shock, with Brent above 100 and more than 70% of its oil already coming from abroad. Rosebank, west of Shetland, is an £8.7 billion (~11.6 billion) development that its operator says would pump about 69,000 barrels a day at peak, roughly a tenth of the country’s expected oil output. The production vessel has been on site since June, and Ithaca Energy, which owns a fifth of the field, says it will likely stop investing in Britain if the government…

articles.title: Beijing Pushes Domestic Oil Production as Iranian Supply Dries Up
articles.description: China needs its biggest oil and gas producers to drill more, explore more, and build strategic supply bases as the Iran war forces Beijing to confront an uncomfortable reality: even the world's largest crude stockpile cannot replace a dependable supply of oil indefinitely. China's National Energy Administration has called on PetroChina, Sinopec, CNOOC, and other domestic producers to expand production capacity, increase investment, and accelerate the development of national oil and gas supply bases. The directive, issued following an October 21…

articles.title: Alleged Russian Funding Prompts Executive Exodus at U.S. LNG Firm
articles.description: The top executives of U.S. energy startup Polar LNG have all resigned in recent weeks, just six months after the company was launched, amid a controversy over alleged funding and control of the venture’s strategy by Russia’s biggest LNG developer and exporter, privately-held Novatek. The senior managers who left Polar LNG say they resigned in September after learning earlier during the month that Novatek was at least partly funding the U.S. company, which looks to build a project on Alaska’s North Slope. Polar LNG was created…

articles.title: Asia Needs $1 Trillion a Year to Avoid the Next Energy Shock
articles.description: Oil and gas may be flowing through the Strait of Hormuz again, but the impacts of its months-long closure will be felt for years to come. For Asia, in particular, regulating markets and shoring up energy security to avoid the next energy shock will require trillions of dollars in the coming years as energy demand projection rates continue to rise sharply across the region. articles.title: Transgaz, Kawasaki Ink Hydrogen Cooperation Agreement
articles.description: Kawasaki Heavy Industries and Transgaz signed a memorandum of understanding on energy cooperation that would see the Japanese company bring its hydrogen transmission technology into Europe.

articles.title: North America Adds Rigs Week on Week, BH Count Shows
articles.description: North America added three rigs week on week, according to Baker Hughes' latest North America rotary rig count.

articles.title: BP Gets New Settlement with Louisiana over Deepwater Horizon Disaster
articles.description: BP reached an agreement with the state of Louisiana that will close lengthy litigation over the deadly Deepwater Horizon catastrophe in the Gulf of America in 2010, in exchange for an early but reduced payment of remaining claims.
